Situation Report on the 17th EBOLA Virus Disease Epidemic /DRC
SitRep N°28/MVB_11/06/2026

Affected provinces (3) ITURI, NORD-KIVU & SUD-KIVU
Affected Health Zones (29)
• Ituri (19/36) : Aru, Aungba, Bambu, Bunia, Damas, Gety, Kilo, Komanda, Lita, Logo, Mambasa, Mangala, Mongbwalu, Nizi, Nyankunde, Rimba, Rwampara, Tchomia, Kambala.
• Nord-Kivu (9/34) : Beni, Butembo, Goma, Kalunguta, Katwa, Kyondo, Oicha, Masereka et Vuhovi.
• Sud-Kivu (1/34) : Miti-Murhesa
Reporting date 11 June 2026
Publication date 12 June 2026

Cumulative confirmed cases for the 3 provinces 689*
Cumulative deaths among confirmed and case fatality rate 139(20,2%)
Patients in isolation - hospitalisation 315(69,7%)

Suspected cases of the day 168(64 deaths)**
Contact follow-up rate for the 3 provinces 28,4%

* *Suspected deaths occurring in the community are undergoing in-depth investigation with a view to possible reclassification (non-cases, probable cases).

## 1. HIGHLIGHTS

• Seventeen (17) new confirmed cases including 5 deaths, were reported on 11 June 2026, in the ZS (health zone) of Bunia (6), Rwampara (5), Mongbwalu (4), Nizi (2) in Ituri province.
• Supervision visit carried out to the CTE (Ebola treatment centre) in the ZS of Butembo and Katwa by the COUSP and the national IM of the response against the 17th epidemic against MVE.
• Arrival of the DG of the INSP (National Institute of Public Health) and the multidisciplinary team (COUSP-OMS) in the Butembo zone to strengthen Response actions in the said ZS and its surroundings.
• Receipt of a cardiac monitor and pulse oximeter at CTE Rwampara.

## 2. EPIDEMIOLOGICAL AND OPERATIONAL CONTEXT

Ituri province, located in the north-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, shares a long and porous border with Uganda and South Sudan.
For more than two decades, it has been confronted with a chronic humanitarian crisis linked to armed conflicts and recurrent population displacements.
Its population is estimated at more than 8 million inhabitants, including more than one million internally displaced persons.
The Mongbwalu health zone, considered the starting point of the epidemic, is located in the Djugu territory 70 km from Bunia.
This zone is characterised by the presence of armed groups, frequent population movements towards Uganda, and numerous artisanal mining sites attracting migrant workers.
In September 2018, Ituri province had already been affected by the 10th MVE epidemic which was then raging in Nord-Kivu.
The current epidemic, due to Bundibugyo ebolavirus, was officially declared on 15 May 2026 by the Minister of Public Health.
The three affected provinces have a total population estimated at nearly 15 million inhabitants, with massive internal displacements and cross-border flows towards neighbouring countries.

[FIGURE: Figure 1. Chronology of events of the Ebola-Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic.]

• No new health zone was affected by the end of the day of 11 June 2026.
Thus, the number of affected ZS remains at 29/104 (section 3.1).
Ituri province remains the epicentre with 93,8% of confirmed cases reported in the 3 affected provinces.
Nord-Kivu province remains the most affected in terms of case fatality (60,0%) whilst Ituri province shows low case fatality (17,6%).
On the other hand, Sud-Kivu province has remained silent since 26 May 2026, the date on which its last confirmed case was reported.

## 3.3 Temporal analysis:

An increasing number of confirmed cases is observed from one week to the next, reflecting continuous transmission of the disease in the community.
A sudden geographical expansion of the epidemic is to be feared if public health actions are not implemented rapidly.

## 4. RESPONSE ACTIONS BY PILLAR

## 4.1 Coordination

National / Ituri :
• Coordination assessment mission in Beni and Butembo as part of the response to the 17th epidemic.
• Since Wednesday, a preparedness briefing on MVE has been underway for all staff of the Hôpital du Cinquantenaire in Kinshasa (management site for MVE cases in Kinshasa).
• Holding of a working session (SGI-PTF-National level expert coordination) in the ZS of Rwampara in order to strengthen epidemiological surveillance aspects, particularly contact listing and follow-up.
• Supervision visit by the COUSP and national IM to the CTE (ZS of Butembo and Katwa).
• Working exchange between the DG of the INSP and the provincial team of the Butembo antenna on strengthening response actions.
• Closing of training for national and provincial SGI members.

## 4.3 Laboratory

• Ituri : 35 new samples collected and analysed (positivity 48,6% ; n=17)
• Nord-Kivu : 172 samples pending in Nord-Kivu (delay > 5 days).

## 4.4 Infection Prevention and Control (PCI)

• Ituri : Start of training for 36 TS and 36 teachers on PCI (infection prevention and control)/ Wash in the ZS of Komanda ; continuation of training (D2) in PCI and EDS (ZS Nyankunde) ; briefing of 10 healthcare providers from 4 ESS on handwashing, bio-cleaning, waste management, donning and doffing of PPE (ZS Bambu) ; briefing of 56 members (community leaders, groupement heads and IT) on MVE and prevention measures ; decontamination of 2 ESS (Clinique Marie Claire : Babenda) and CH Rwankole) and 2 households of confirmed cases (Q/ Bigo and Lembabo) ; briefing of 3 healthcare providers from CS Komanda on handwashing.
• Nord-Kivu : Assessment of 4 ESS (CH FEPSI : 61%, CH SHANGILIENI : 48%, CH KYAGHALA 68 % and Dispensaire la Charité 15%) ; 2/2 ESS decontaminated (HGR (general referral hospital) Katwa and CH FEPSI) ; 46/56 providers briefed on PCI themes across 14/17 supported ESS ; exposure risk assessment of 15/36 providers in ESS of the ZS of Katwa(CH Kyaghala) and Butembo (CH FEPSI, CH Shangilieni and CH La vérité (among PPL (person released from treatment (discharged patient)) : 11 at high risk, 3 at intermediate risk and 1 at low risk ; 26 supported ESS in the ZS of Goma, Karisimbi and Nyiragongo with 29 providers briefed on the different themes of PCI.
• Sud-Kivu : Decontamination of 12 households and 9 latrines around a contact who became suspected in AS (health area) Kabushwa ; support to the EIR (donning and doffing) for 6 samples taken including 2 in AS Kahungu, 1 in AS Lwiro and 3 in AS Kabushwa ; theoretical and practical briefing of 6 hygienists from CS Kahungu on the "3 buckets" decontamination technique ; accompaniment of the 2 CS (Kahungu and Kalagane) where 12 providers were briefed on standard PCI precaution measures in hospital settings.

## 4.6 Continuity of services.

• Assessment of 5 ESS of the Nizi health zone.
• Production of recovery plans for already assessed ESS.

## 4.7 Risk communication and community engagement

Nord-Kivu : 11 853 people sensitised in public spaces and strategic points, strengthening prevention and community trust in favour of MVE response measures ; 77 key community actors including 41 women and 36 men including community leaders and influencers engaged to improve dissemination of reliable messages and adherence to the response in their sermons ; 18 radio stations produced 18 broadcasts and 36 spots with massive dissemination of messages via these local radio stations on prevention, signs of MVE and hand hygiene ; 11 community alerts reported with the involvement of 368 community actors, thus strengthening surveillance and early warning in communities.
Sud-Kivu : Advocacy with 45 leaders of the Katana health zone on their involvement in the fight against Ebola virus disease ; holding of the CREC pillar meeting in the Mitimurhesa health zone on interventions to be carried out around MVE cases ; briefing of 10 CREC pillar members selected from the different strata of the community in the Katana health zone.
Ituri : Evaluation of MVE response activities in the ZS Mongbwalu under the chairmanship of the AT of Djugu ; advocacy with the Bourgmestre of the Commune of SHARI for their involvement in regulating prayers in the enclosure of the Balidja mortuary not far from CME/Nyankunde, ZS Rwampara.
Observation : Funeral prayers for the release of deceased bodies are organised inside this mortuary and brass bands are used on this occasion.
Result : The Bourgmestre promised to invite the owner of this mortuary to summon them in accordance with instructions from the provincial Governor.
Support to other pillars :
• Surveillance : investigation and listing of contact cases (ZS Bunia, AS BIGO) ;
• PCI : preparing families to adhere to EDS in case of community deaths (ZS Bunia, AS Bankoko and Bigo).
Result : EDS performed.

## 4.8 Logistics and Security

• Receipt of medicines and delivery of PCI supplies, medicines to the ZS of Rwampara
• Delivery of equipment CTE/CME-Bunia.

## 4.9. Security

• The security situation in the city of Bunia (Bunia and Rwampara health zones) is relatively calm.
However, the activism of armed groups in the territories of Djugu, Irumu and Mambasa continues to limit humanitarian access in several affected or at-risk health zones.

## 4.10. PSEA (Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse)

• In Ituri : With support from WFP cooperating partners, 74 participants (31 women and 43 men) took part in activities organised in Bunia.
Furthermore, 27 participants (10 women and 17 men), including FHI360 staff, proceeded to sign the code of conduct.
Finally, a session with community leaders mobilised 77 participants (30 women and 47 men).
• Nord-Kivu : In Goma and in Béni : organisation of sensitisation sessions for the second wave of community relays and community leaders 155 people took part in these activities, including 71 women, 53 participants (13 women and 40 men) of whom 21 signed the code (5F and 16M).
• Sud-Kivu : PSEA briefing for the benefit of actors intervening in the response as well as healthcare providers from CS Kabushwa, in total 42 people (13 women) ; PSEA briefing of 100 (31 women) teachers from ZS of Mitimurhesa (Lwiro) on SEA concepts, reporting mechanism followed by the signing of code of conduct.

## 5. MAIN CHALLENGES


| No. | Challenges | Impact | Required action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reluctance towards post-mortem sampling (swabs) | Delay in confirmation; underestimation of cases | Intensive community engagement; involvement of religious leaders |
| 2 | Insufficient capacity in standard CTEs despite the opening of Rwampara | Potential saturation of existing CTEs | Acceleration of the construction of planned CTEs |
| 4 | Failure in supply of Essential Generic Medicines (MEG) in targeted HGRs | Weakening of overall care management | Advocacy for MEG allocation |
| 5 | Shortage of PCI supplies (PPE, DLM, chlorine) in Nord-Kivu | Nosocomial risk | Urgent supply |
| 6 | Low escalation of alerts in the 3 provinces | Delay in case detection | Strengthening of community surveillance |
| 7 | Insufficient financial resources for all pillars | Slowdown of operations | Resource mobilisation (gap of 21,5 million USD) |
